text: This report provides information on the status of the City’s health and safety system, specifically performance for 2020 and actions and priorities to address identified hazards. There was a 9.7 percent increase in the number of lost time injuries in 2020 relative to 2019. This increase was primarily due to workplace exposures to COVID-19. There was a decrease in lost time injuries across all other categories primarily due to a delay in the resumption of services or decreased service delivery as a result of COVID-19. There was a 45.7 percent decrease in the number of recurrences and a 36.0 percent decrease in the number of medical aid injuries in 2020 relative to 2019. The overall invoiced costs related to the City's current Workplace Safety and Insurance Board firm number increased from $32.3 million in 2019 to $38.3 million in 2020.
